look_here_first: Start with the big asymmetric leaf and the spring samara: American elm has relatively large double-serrate leaves with a strongly uneven base, then a flat oval samara with a ciliate margin and a deep apical notch.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: large deciduous elm, often developing a vase-shaped crown

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: leaves mostly >7 cm, ovate to elliptic with strongly oblique base

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: lower leaf surface glabrous to pubescent, often with tufts in vein axils

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: flowers before leaf-out in spring on slender pedicels

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: oval spring samara with seed near center, ciliate margin, and a deep apical notch

lookalikes.differences: Ulmus rubra: Slippery elm has red-tomentose bud-scale margins, much rougher thick leaves, and a samara pubescent on the body rather than a ciliate margin. Ulmus alata: Winged elm has smaller leaves and conspicuous regular corky wings on branches; American elm lacks those wings. Ulmus crassifolia: Cedar elm has much smaller rough leaves and reproduces in fall rather than spring.
